convictions.notes: CONTESTED, and the disagreement is not trivial. The tier-1 appellate opinion concerns a single count of murder with malice and a single life sentence. Two 2020 news reports state he was serving six life sentences, which is also the number of counts on which Henley was convicted — a coincidence that makes conflation the most likely explanation, but 'most likely' is not a finding. Until a TDCJ commitment record or the trial court's judgments are obtained, this record does not assert a number. The tier-1 source is given primacy in confirmed_victim_count for that reason.

confirmed_victim_count.notes: One is the count established by the only judgment this record has read. If the six-life-sentences reports are right, this field is wrong by five, and any analyst using it should treat it as provisional. Recorded as contested rather than silently taking the higher or the lower figure. This is the single most important open question on the record. Note also that under docs/co-offenders.md this count is never summed with Henley's six or with the twenty-seven recoveries: they are different judicial findings about one series, not disjoint sets of victims.

claimed_victim_count.notes: Recorded as a datum about what Brooks said, never as a victim count, per the schema. It is an estimate of the SERIES, not of his own conduct, and it was given by an eighteen-year-old the day after the series ended. The recoveries that followed — twenty-seven — fall inside his range, which is corroboration of a kind and is worth noting precisely because it is so rare in this literature. It still is not a count.

estimate_provenance.value: Series totals of 27, 28 and 29 circulate and are routinely attached to Brooks as though they were findings against him. The 27 is the number of bodies recovered in 1973 per the appellate record; the 28 is the number of sets of remains counted in later Houston reporting; the 29 appears in feature coverage without a stated basis.

victim_selection.notes: The retrieved opinion describes Brooks's role as presence and assistance rather than procurement — his own account was that he 'was supposed to help if something went wrong' and that he assisted in burying bodies. It attributes no selection function to him. Recording a selection pattern here would import Henley's role onto Brooks, which is precisely the error separate records exist to prevent. Null by design.

signature_behaviour.notes: No scene documentation or post-mortem finding establishing recurrent non-necessary conduct attributable to Brooks was located. The torture described in the opinions is attributed to the offences generally, not to him individually, and derives from confession evidence in any case. Null.

motive_classification.notes: Deliberately null. The only motive material in the record is Brooks's own characterisation of his role, given in custody at eighteen the day after the series ended, in circumstances where minimising his own part was the obvious interest. Coding a motive from that would be coding a defence. Compare USA-010-BERKOWITZ, also left null, where the only motive evidence is an account the offender later repudiated. Holmes & Holmes offers no category for a subordinate participant; see the note on USA-012-HENLEY for what happens when one is forced.

spatial_pattern.notes: Not coded. Canter & Larkin's commuter/marauder distinction models the relationship between an offender's home base and his own offence locations. Brooks did not select or approach victims on the record retrieved, so there is no offender-specific spatial behaviour to code, and applying the series pattern to him would attribute conduct the record does not support. Null by design, not for want of searching.

weapon_or_method.notes: The opinions describe victims being shot or strangled, but do not establish a method attributable to Brooks individually, and his own statement placed him in an assisting role. confession_reliability.value: Partly corroborated at series level, unestablished at count level. Brooks's estimate of 'between 25 and thirty boys' was consistent with the twenty-seven bodies subsequently recovered, and the recoveries followed disclosures by both men. What independently corroborated his statement as to the count he was convicted of has not been established from the retrieved opinion.

confession_reliability.notes: The distinction between series-level and count-level corroboration is the point. That a confession is accurate about the scale of a series does not establish that it is accurate about who did what within it — and apportionment among participants is exactly what a confession given in custody is least reliable about, since each participant has an interest in the allocation. USA-003-HALL is the case where no corroboration existed at all; this is a case where it exists at one level and is unverified at the other.
